steps.content: You peruse through the file in your hands. It's about a homicide case caused by inheritance disputes.
Technically, this isn't the MBCC's responsibility, but because the accused is a Sinner, she has been transferred to your care before the trial.
After carefully reviewing all the information, only one thought pops into your mind: this case has been handled too hastily.
Whether out of routine or your responsibility as caretaker, you decide to conduct an Interrogation to understand the details of the case.
Nice to meet you, Mrs. Garofano-Braun. I'm the MBCC Chief, ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Hello, Chief. Please, just call me by my first name. I never actually changed my surname.
The widow before you looks somewhat frail, but even though she's incarcerated and burdened by her husband's murder, a soft, gentle smile still graces her face.
I see. All right then, Garofano. Please relax. I'm just here to... ask you a few questions.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I promise to tell you whatever you want to know.

Let's review the case first, Garofano.
You pull out the documents from the file folder, laying them out one by one.
After Mr. Braun's sudden death from a critical illness, his will stipulates that all his wealth should go to you, his widow.
However, at this juncture, someone not only anonymously reported you as a Sinner, but also accused you of murdering your husband for his wealth in court.
At their strong insistence, the authorities conducted an autopsy on Mr. Braun's body.
According to the autopsy, an unidentified puncture wound was found in a hidden part of the deceased's body. A lethal, slow-acting poison was extracted from it.
Subsequently, they sealed off your tailor shop and found the murder weapon that matched both the wound and the poison. You were arrested based on this evidence. After that...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: After that, I ended up here.
A hint of melancholy tints Garofano's smile.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Chief, you've been very thorough. You've read all the information carefully.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: But that... isn't the whole truth.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I'm not the one who murdered Mr. Braun.
Her voice trembles, but her tone is firm.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: But as soon as they found out that I'm a Sinner, they jumped to the conclusion that I was the culprit, without giving me any chance to prove my innocence...

The sentencing was too swift, and there was practically no procedural process. They even let someone anonymous who wasn't family to ask for an autopsy. It was like... they were playing some childish game.
It makes no sense to sentence someone on such scattered evidence.
I don't think that being a "Sinner" should automatically condemn someone to guilt.
Garofano then says something somewhat unexpected.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I thought you were also here to persuade me to accept my sentence...
The truth of the matter will ultimately be revealed. I don't categorically believe or disbelieve you. I just think that only after knowing the full picture can one make the final judgment.
So, I'd like to hear your side of the story before making my judgment.
She gently nods, then starts to speak.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: All right, then... here is my side of the story.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: In reality, Mr. Braun and I weren't married in a legal sense.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: We were more like brother and sister than husband and wife.
A de facto companionship?

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Yes, you could say that.
She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear, immersing herself into deeper memories.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Mr. Braun was passionate about charity, and I was an orphan girl he helped.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I lost my whole family in a Mania attack. I was the only one left... I barely survived.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Although I also became a Sinner because of this, at least... I didn't turn into... a monster that can't even recognize its own family.
A trace of pain flashes across her face, but she quickly suppresses it.
Sorry, I didn't mean to make you remember these things.
You gently hand a tissue to Garofano. A faint smile surfaces on her face.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I know, Chief.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: At the time, I felt helpless, and almost lost the will to live... but fortunately, I met Mr. Braun.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: He didn't care that I was a Sinner, and gave me a lot of earnest help. He even funded me to open a tailor shop, which got my life back on track.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I was very grateful for this and always wanted to repay him.
Is this why you had a sham marriage with Mr. Braun?

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Yes. Mr. Braun was sickly and needed someone to take care of him all the time. I always helped Mrs. Braun with housework when I had time...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Later, Mrs. Braun fell ill. Before she passed away, she asked me to move in to keep taking care of Mr. Braun.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: As his wife, I also went to burdensome social events in his place. All of this was voluntary.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: We lived like family, watching over and caring for each other. I thought that life would always be so calm and cozy, until...
Garofano can't help but let out a sob.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: ...Sorry about that.
I understand... it's not easy to lose a family member.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Then you should also understand... having lost my family once, I couldn't bear that kind of heart-wrenching pain again.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I... cherished them very much. I would rather die myself than see my family leave me...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: That feeling is like.. being abandoned to be all alone in this world...
She pauses for a moment, unable to suppress her sorrow any longer... Tears trickle down her cheeks, leaving a faint shining trace.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Ah... Thank you.
As Garofano takes the tissue, you brush against her icy fingertips, which feel somewhat rough and callused.
After a moment, she collects herself, and slowly raises her head to look at you seriously.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I know... everyone thinks I'm the cruel murderer, but I...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: ...would never harm my own family.
Garofano's immense grief pours into your consciousness through the shackles... but beneath that tide of pain, there is resolute determination.
You don't want to believe that someone so passionate would lie about her innocence.
But, given the current evidence, the odds are stacked against you.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Hmm, I know.
Garofano flashes a bitter smile.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: If you think I was after his money... I can tell you, we had an agreement. I wouldn't inherit any property from Mr. Braun.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Besides, even if that agreement is non-binding, the order of inheritance stipulates that his younger brother—the younger Mr. Braun—would be the one to inherit his estate.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: As for his will... I only found out about it after his death.
A younger brother...? You recall the case file you saw, which didn't mention Mr. Braun having a younger brother.

But the file was vague about the complainant from start to finish. You thought it might have been a neighbor who was unwilling to disclose their personal information. But now that you think about it, it seems...
You need to find a way to investigate this.
Seeing you fall silent, Garofano lowers her eyes and speaks softly.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: But actually, I no longer have any hopes about correcting this misunderstanding.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: As long as someone can listen to my story, I'm happy.

options: I can help you if you want.

choices.text: I can help you if you want.

steps.content: Although the truth about the case is still unclear, I'm willing to trust you this once. I'm willing to believe how much you cherish your "family."
Garofano stares at you in surprise.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: So you mean... you're willing to believe I'm innocent?
I can only promise you that I will find out what really happened.
Plus, I know the public is biased against Sinners. But we can't rush to conclusions and ignore the truth.
So, I will apply to defer the trial and look for evidence that can clear your name. This is the only way to prove your innocence.
Before that happens, I hope you can trust me too.
Garofano freezes. She seems to be stunned to hear you say this. After a moment, she begins to speak softly.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Chief, you... remind me of someone.
An emotional, nostalgic look crosses her face. You instantly realize something.
...A family member?
Garofano nods slowly.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: My younger brother.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: He was just like you, kind and righteous...
steps.female_content: She was just like you, kind and righteous...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: He always wanted to be like our father, a proud and selfless member of the FAC.
steps.female_content: She always wanted to be like our father, a proud and selfless member of the FAC.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Such a pity...
Her voice trails off, the unfinished words dissipating into the air.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I'm lucky to meet someone as righteous as you...

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: I am really... grateful that you are doing this for me.
You are my Sinner. It is my duty to investigate everything about you.
This is my responsibility. So, you really don't have to thank me.
Garofano nods in agreement and laughs lightly.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: ...All right, dutiful Chief.
For now, just rest at ease at the MBCC.
I won't let those people bother you.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: Understood. I will just stay here...
She gives a gentle but formal bow.

steps.speaker: Garofano
steps.content: ...and wait for you patiently.
